query: Your Name on It {f} is running a stall at the next fair, selling enchanted bookmarks to pay for next year's books, and has had an idea: what if the sign said "as used by {player}"? You have, in fact, used one. Once. "It'd sell out in an hour," {f} says. "Go on. I can't afford the set texts otherwise." Let {f} use your name The stall sells out in forty minutes, and {f} can buy every book on next year's list, with enough over for a new quill. {f} is giddy all evening. You're asked to sign three bookmarks, and you do, and one of them ends up in the library, where it marks a page for years. The sign draws a crowd, and then the bookmarks start marking the wrong pages, all of them, at once. People bring them back in handfuls, saying your name in a tone you don't like. {f} is mortified. You help pack up the stall. Help at the stall instead You say your name stays off the sign, but you'll spend the afternoon behind the stall. You sell twenty bookmarks, badly, and {f} sells two hundred, very well. It's one of the nicest afternoons of the term.
